title: lore check and sync take an advisory lock per git common dir, with result reuse and stale-holder recovery
description: DEC-282 item 2, filed from ODOC-610 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z). VERBATIM: 'lore-cli: an advisory lock per git common dir for check and sync. A waiter with matching tree hashes reuses the finished result, and a stale holder never blocks forever.' CONTEXT from the report: four to five concurrent runs made about 45 quest processes and a load of about 128, and on 2026-11-12 that shut the fleet down; any quest write staled the lore:tasks rollup, so lore check exited 6 and everyone re-ran sync and check defensively. The lock must span worktrees of one clone, which is why it lives in the git common dir rather than the checkout. Ships in the next lore/quest pair (DEC-282 items 1-4 ship together).

acceptanceCriteria.text: check and sync take an advisory lock in the git common dir, so worktrees of one clone contend on the same lock.
A waiter whose tree hashes match a finished result reuses that result instead of recomputing.
A stale holder never blocks a waiter forever; the recovery is measured and bounded.
Both ways: two concurrent runs produce one compute and one reuse, and a stale lock is recovered rather than hanging.
Measured at about 2000 tasks: concurrent runs no longer multiply quest processes.

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES — opum-ai/lore-cli#746 (LCLI-792) at 57773ea0f012874095b9c2eb3c0e5b0a02d7f817
Findings (file:line at HEAD 57773ea0):
1. BLOCKING — the stale-lock steal has the same race class as the quest-cli#760 bug, and nothing serialises it. src/core/advisory-lock.ts:422-424 and 558-570. `inspectLock` decides "stale". Then `stealLock` renames whatever file is at the path at that moment and unlinks it. There is no `.break` O_EXCL mutex, and nothing re-reads the lock to check it still matches the record that was judged stale. Interleaving, with no crash needed beyond the original dead holder: Holder A is dead. Waiters B and C both inspect it and see "stale". C steals, `continue`s, and creates its own lock (now live). B runs `stealLock`, moves C's LIVE lock aside, unlinks it, then creates its own. Result: two holders computing at once. C's heartbeat (:532) and release (:546) see owner≠C and go silent, but C's compute continues. With 4-5 waiters polling every 50 ms after a crash (the incident shape), several of them see "stale" in the same window. Two smaller instances of the same class: heartbeat :531-537: read owner, then `renameSync(tmp, path)`. A steal-and-create between those two steps gets the new holder's lock overwritten with the old owner's record. `releaseLock` :546-549: read, then unlink. It can unlink a successor's lock. Fix shape (quest's id-allocation lock): breakers serialise on an O_EXCL `<lock>.break` file, which needs its own stale bound. Under it, re-read the lock and unlink only if owner+updatedAt still equal what was judged stale. Nothing is parked or restored. Heartbeat and release should also re-verify under the break file, or use a per-owner file plus a link-based protocol.
2. BLOCKING — a live, busy holder loses its lock by design. advisory-lock.ts:478-487 and :529. On the same host, a live pid with a well-formed identity is still put through the age test (`now - updatedAt > 15 s` → stale). The heartbeat is a `setInterval` on the same event loop as `compute`. Much of `runCheck` is synchronous: the schema pass, `loadAgentProfiles`/`loadBundle`, capacity measurement, and `Bun.spawnSync` git calls in adapters/git.ts. `runCheck` can even return a number synchronously (src/commands/check.ts:202, 226). Any synchronous stretch over 15 s, plausible at load ~58-128, makes a running holder look stale, and with finding 1 that produces two holders. Laptop suspend/resume and a forward wall-clock step (both `updatedAt` and `deadline` use `Date.now`) do the same. A backward step stretches the 120 s cap. Suggest: on the same host with the pid alive, never steal by age, and leave wedged-but-alive to the hard cap. Use age only for other-host or unprovable records. Note also that `processStartIdentity` is only regex-checked (:490-495) and never compared against the live process, so a reused pid counts as alive. That is bounded, but the "start identity" defends against nothing.
3. BLOCKING — reusing `sync` across worktrees skips the waiter's writes. advisory-lock.ts:209 and :237 hash `root` RELATIVE to the toplevel, never the toplevel itself. Two worktrees of one clone at the same HEAD with the same diff hash identically. That is common: clean worktrees at one SHA, or reviewer worktrees. A `lore sync` waiting in worktree B then replays A's "wrote N files" stdout and exit code while writing NOTHING into B. The ruling's "reuses the finished result" holds only when the result's side effects landed in the waiter's tree. test/advisory-lock.test.ts ("two callers rooted in DIFFERENT worktrees…", diff hunk ~line 110) pins cross-worktree reuse as intended, but with resultName "check" and a fake hash, so this case is never exercised. Fix: include the canonical toplevel in the key for `sync` at least, or disable reuse for any non-dry-run sync. For `check`, cross-worktree reuse is correct only if no rendered output names an absolute path. I could not confirm that either way.
4. NON-BLOCKING (borderline) — the 120 s hard cap brings the storm back at the scale AC 4 names. advisory-lock.ts:427-432. The deadline is absolute from each caller's start, not per holder or per progress. Take N worktrees at different HEADs: different hashes, so no reuse, and runs strictly serialise. If any run takes more than about 120/N s, every waiter past the cap computes UNLOCKED at the same moment. The task records 83 s at 574 tasks before LCLI-791, and AC 4 says "measured at about 2000 tasks". Suggest resetting the deadline whenever the holder's owner changes, so a cap applies per wedged holder rather than per queue position. All three forced paths are silent: mkdir failure :362-366, create "error" :395-399, and max-wait. `advisory-run.ts:118-129` ignores `outcome.forced`. Emit one stderr advisory line when coordination is abandoned, and another while waiting, since a silent wait of up to 120 s reads as a hang. On Windows, `openSync("wx")` against a pending-delete or being-renamed file can return EPERM rather than EEXIST, and that goes straight to the silent unlocked "error" path (I could not verify this).
5. NON-BLOCKING — scope and output behaviour. The ruling does not ask for end-of-run output. Output is buffered even when `reusable:false` (advisory-run.ts:123, capture at :134), so serialised `--external` runs and all injected-seam runs lose progressive output for no reuse benefit. Effects: Ctrl-C or SIGTERM mid-sync loses ALL output. The catch at :143 only covers thrown errors. stdout/stderr interleaving collapses to all-stdout-then-all-stderr (:148-151). That is visible under `2>&1`. Exit codes are preserved. I checked that check.ts and sync.ts send every `emit`/`flush` to the passed sinks (check.ts:336, 412-473; sync.ts:216, 276, 296, 355), so capture is complete and a replay is byte-identical to the holder's own output. The buffering Writer has no `.columns` or `.isTTY`; check and sync don't read either from the sink, so rendering is unchanged. This is a user-visible design choice beyond the ruling. Under the design-authority rule it should go to opum-doc rather than being settled in the PR. At minimum, buffer only when the run is reusable.
6. NON-BLOCKING — the hash leaves out some inputs that are not on disk. QUEST_TIMEOUT / QUEST_ACTOR* env (adapters/quest.ts:263, 284-286), the backlog timeout env (adapters/backlog.ts:126), and the resolved quest binary or version are all omitted. Within one clone and session the risk is low, but the CHANGELOG's "any changed input recomputes" overclaims. Thrown failures (LoreError) are never cached (advisory-run.ts:143-145), so waiters behind a throwing holder each recompute serially. That is correct, but it reduces the benefit. Exit-6/7 report outcomes are returned (check.ts:962-971), so those ARE reused. That covers the incident case.
7. NON-BLOCKING — residue. Result slots in `<common>/lore/advisory/*.result.json` keep the full last stdout/stderr indefinitely, with default umask perms; only the lock file is 0600. A failed heartbeat rename leaves `<lock>.<owner>.tmp` behind (:535-536). A failed unlink leaves `.stale.<owner>` (:561-565). If `writeFileSync` in `tryCreateLock` throws (ENOSPC), the error propagates out of the command and leaves an empty lock that is judged by mtime: it recovers after 15 s, but the command fails instead of falling back. Nothing ever sweeps the directory. A killed holder's lock is recovered by the dead-pid probe (good).
8. NON-BLOCKING — the tests do not exercise any of the blocking paths. Every test runs in-process under one pid with an injected clock. `isProcessAlive` is always mocked, so `defaultIsProcessAlive` never runs. Missing tests: two concurrent stealers of one stale lock, a real cross-process exclusion test (two `lore` processes), a real kill -9 of a holder, a heartbeat starved by a synchronous compute, and a cross-worktree sync reuse. The "3 red" mutation covers only the reuse branch. The steal path has no guard for a mutation to remove. AC 4 ("measured at about 2000 tasks: concurrent runs no longer multiply quest processes") has no measurement in the PR and is still owed.
Could not verify without a shell: how long the synchronous stretches of check/sync actually run under load, i.e. whether finding 2 fires in practice rather than only in principle; Windows `openSync("wx")` EPERM/EBUSY on a pending-delete file, `renameSync` over an open file, and `process.kill(pid,0)` semantics; whether check's rendered output contains absolute paths, which decides whether cross-worktree `check` reuse is also wrong; whether sync on a clean, already-synced HEAD is a byte-for-byte no-op, which would make finding 3 harmless when the shared tree is already synced; the writer's 24-test and 3-red mutation numbers (I did not run them); whether any other code already uses `<git-common-dir>/lore/`.

== RESIDUAL (c): the mechanism and the exposure ==

1. What the waiter checks before it writes
- advisory-run.ts:142 computes the entry hash ONCE, before withAdvisoryResult is called.
- advisory-lock.ts:592 → :584-589 is the while-waiting reuse test. It requires slot.inputHash === that entry hash, and finishedAt > startedAt. The tree is not rehashed on this path. `rehash` (:615) runs only on the path where the waiter acquires the lock itself.
- The reuse is returned at :594. advisory-run.ts:165-166 then calls applySyncWritePlan (sync.ts:396-413), which runs:
  - assertNoSymlinkInAnyPath (path shape only: no symlinked ancestor),
  - ensureDir,
  - readFileIfPresent for each file's `before` (:407), which feeds the rollback and is compared with nothing,
  - writeManyAtomicOrRollback (:409),
  - the tracker sweep.
- SyncWritePlan is only {path, after} (sync.ts:145-147, recorded at :341). It holds no pre-image and no digest. At apply time, nothing can tell an edited file from an unedited one.

2. Which files it can overwrite
Every path in plan.writes, under <waiter-root>/docs/. Each file is replaced whole with the holder's bytes:
- every concept doc whose managed task block or task-rollup field changed,
- every regenerated index.md whose bytes changed,
- docs/log.md.

Nothing outside the plan is touched: no backlog/, no .quest/, no docs file that is not in the plan. The material loss is in concept docs. A real sync re-reads each one fresh and rewrites only the block and the rollup field, so an edit to the body or other frontmatter survives (LORE-119, sync.ts:268-279). The plan carries the holder's whole-file bytes, so that edit is reverted. index.md and log.md are generated anyway, but a HEAD move or a new concept during the wait still lands a stale log.md or index.md, where a recompute would have included it.

3. Exposure window
- It opens at advisory-run.ts:142, the entry hash.
- It stays open through the entire poll loop (advisory-lock.ts:591-673): the holder's remaining compute, and with the F4 reset (:641-647) any number of holders, each bounded by 660 s.
- It closes at the write at sync.ts:409.
- The `before` read at :407 changes nothing about this.
- So it is the whole wait plus the apply: typically the holder's remaining run time (seconds to tens of seconds), and in principle more than 11 minutes. The docblock at sync.ts:388-390 ("edited in the instant between hashing and applying") understates it.

4. Same-worktree case
The holder has ALREADY written those files into the waiter's own tree. An edit made after the holder's write and before the waiter's apply is reverted to the holder's bytes. That is exactly the shape a hook-fired sync hits while an agent edits a doc.

5. Would the rollback or the preflight catch the edit? No.
- writeManyAtomicOrRollback rolls back only when a write throws (fswrite.ts:557-570). A successful apply silently replaces the edit. Reading `before` fresh only means a FAILED apply restores the edited bytes.
- The preflight checks symlink ancestry only.

6. The apply also runs OUTSIDE the lock
withAdvisoryResult has already returned when the apply starts. On the reuse path at :594 the waiter never held the lock; on the late-reuse path, :627-630 has already released it. Two consequences:
- (i) A check holder in the waiter's worktree can read a half-applied write set. That contradicts the CHANGELOG's "check and sync share it so a check never reads a half-written tree".
- (ii) A waiter stalled after it returns can apply a stale plan over the output of a newer sync holder that computed from newer .quest state.

7. Conformance with (a7) item 2
I read it as NOT conforming. It meets the letter: writes do land in the waiter's worktree. But item 2 defines what is reused as "the batched task read and the rendered blocks FOR MATCHING INPUTS". The implementation:
- checks "matching" only against a snapshot taken before the wait, and
- reuses whole-file bytes, including content that was never part of the computation (doc bodies and other frontmatter, read from the holder's tree at the holder's time).

That breaks a guarantee the existing code already gives (LORE-119), so I would not call it a design choice.

8. Smallest apply-time verification, and the trap to avoid
- The naive fix kills reuse: "rehash at apply and require it to equal slot.inputHash". In the SAME worktree, the holder's own writes (sync.ts:342) change the tree after its keyHash (advisory-lock.ts:615). So whenever the plan is non-empty, that check always mismatches, and same-worktree sync waiters silently degrade to serial recompute. No test would catch that: the only sync-reuse test (lcli792:344) is cross-worktree.
- Minimum that works: carry each file's holder-side `before` (bytes or digest, absence included) in the plan. At apply time, require each target's current bytes to equal `after` (already applied, so skip) or `before` (so write). Anything else abandons reuse and recomputes. Do the compare and the write UNDER the lock, which also closes item 6.
- Complete version: the slot records both the pre-write and the post-write input hash, and the waiter accepts either. That also covers stale log.md and index.md from a HEAD or concept change.
- Tests to pair with it:
  - a same-worktree sync waiter that asserts computes === 1, and
  - an edit to a plan file during the wait that survives.

== NEW FINDINGS ==

BLOCKING
- Residual (c), above.

SHOULD-FIX

1. advisory-lock.ts:939: `unlinkSync(ctx.breakPath)` on an aged `.break` is not quiet about ENOENT.
   - Scenario: a stale lock plus a stranded `.break` (a breaker, or a holder killed in the heartbeat/release window). N waiters poll every 50 ms and cross breakStaleMs together. Two of them read the file, judge it stale, and both unlink it. The loser gets ENOENT, which takeBreakFile throws, :987-988 turns into "error", and :652-659 runs that waiter UNLOCKED, beside the winner, printing "cannot break the stale lock … (ENOENT…)".
   - That is a lost race reported as a broken mechanism, against (a8). In the heartbeat path it is a missed beat; in the release path the lock is left behind until the 30 s floor.
   - Fix: treat ENOENT there as "wait".

2. A real expiry prints TWO stderr lines, against (a8)'s "ONE line".
   - The waiting notice fires on the first contended poll (:668-671), and the unlocked line fires later (:663-665). Only the latter is (a8)'s line.
   - The command-level test lcli792:409 uses maxWaitMs:0, so expiry fires at :663 before the waiting notice at :668. It measured a configuration the claim is not about.
   - The waiting line also fires on every contended run, even a 50 ms wait. With hook-fired syncs that is routine stderr noise.
   - Your F4 asked for the waiting line, so this is a reconciliation for you or opum-doc. Options: suppress "waiting" once "unlocked" fires, or delay "waiting" by a second or two.

3. advisory-run.ts:213-216: the replay writes all of stdout, then all of stderr.
   - Each stream is byte-identical, but the combined order is not.
   - sync flushes bundle advisories to stderr (sync.ts:235) before its stdout report (:378). Under `2>&1`, the holder shows advisories first and the waiter shows the report first.
   - (a7) item 1 says "replays … byte for byte". Fix: record an ordered list of [stream, chunk].

4. An (a8) "unreadable common dir" can run SILENTLY unlocked.

Q1, a sync waiter's whole-file replay: A, fixed in 0.15.1. Measured at 99f60974: the plan carries only {path, after}, the waiter's match is an input hash taken before its wait, and the apply runs outside the lock. So an edit made during the wait is silently reverted, which breaks LORE-119, and a check holder can read a half-applied tree. That violates (a7) item 2 ("reuse the COMPUTATION only ... never skipping the waiter's own writes" means never overwriting them either). The fix:
- the plan carries each file's holder-side pre-image digest, absence included;
- the apply runs UNDER the lock;
- a file is written only if its current bytes equal the pre-image, and skipped if they already equal `after`;
- any other state abandons reuse and recomputes;
- two tests: computes===1 for a same-worktree sync waiter, and an edit to a plan file made during the wait survives.
Do not "rehash the whole tree and require the input hash": in the same worktree it always mismatches, and degrades reuse silently. B (ship as is, with a CHANGELOG line) is not chosen, because it ships silent data loss in the hook-plus-agent shape the fleet runs every day.

QCLI-563's own measured cold run is 619-623 s, more than 10 minutes. So under quest's rule a waiter BREAKS a healthy cold holder at about 600 s and recomputes concurrently. That is exactly the multiplication item 8 exists to stop, at the scale cont1 reported, and it defeats (a13) item 3(a).
